description: What ENVO, IUCN GET and AGROVOC say about every class domain/land_use_anchors.py cites. Generated by tools/resolve_land_anchors.py; a test compares the module against this, so a mistyped accession fails offline. ENVO types the terrestrial cover, GET the aquatic cover, AGROVOC the regime.

ENVO_00000010.label: transport feature
ENVO_00000010.definition: A construction which enables the movement of humans, their animals or their vehicles.

ENVO_00000043.label: wetland area
ENVO_00000043.definition: An vegetated area which overlaps a wetland ecosystem.

ENVO_00000046.label: hedge
ENVO_00000046.definition: A dense growth of shrubbery planted as a fence or boundary.

ENVO_00000064.label: road
ENVO_00000064.definition: An open way for the passage of vehicles, persons, or animals on land.

ENVO_00000065.label: railway
ENVO_00000065.definition: A permanent way having one or more rails which provides a track for cars.

ENVO_00000106.label: grassland area
ENVO_00000106.definition: An area in which grasses (Graminae) are a significant component of the vegetation.

ENVO_00000111.label: forested area
ENVO_00000111.definition: The definitions of forest can vary greatly, and different classes will be needed to support the major categories. Tree cover alone is not enough to distinguish between forests and plantations. The international definition proposed by the 2010 FAO Forestry Resource Assessment: "land spanning more than 0.5 ha with trees higher than 5 metres and canopy cover of more than 10 percent, or trees able to reach these thresholds in situ . It does not include land that is predominantly under agricultural or urban land use." - FAO.  2010. Global forest resources assessment 2010, Main report, FAO Forestry Paper 163. Rome.

ENVO_00000284.label: quarry
ENVO_00000284.definition: An open-pit mine from which rock or minerals are extracted.

ENVO_00000300.label: scrubland area
ENVO_00000300.definition: Area covered with low-growing or stunted perennial vegetation and usually not mixed with trees.

ENVO_00000533.label: landfill
ENVO_00000533.definition: A depression which contains objects and materials discarded by humans or their technologies.

ENVO_01000228.label: tropical moist broadleaf forest biome
ENVO_01000228.definition: A tropical moist broadleaf forest in which dominant ecological communities have reached their climax successional state.

ENVO_01000311.label: cultivated environment
ENVO_01000311.definition: A cultivated environment is an environment that has been modified by humans by the preparation of the land, usually for the purposes of growing crops.

ENVO_01000746.label: area of perennial ice or snow
ENVO_01000746.definition: According to the NLCD 2011, these areas are characterised by ice and/or snow cover generally greater than 25% of total cover. The definition of perennial needs clarification.

parents.label: fiat part of an astronomical object

ENVO_01000752.label: area of barren land
ENVO_01000752.definition: According to the NLCD 2011, areas of barren land generally have less than 15% cover of vegetation. A specific threshold is not asserted in this definition.

ENVO_01000886.label: area of developed space with high usage intensity
ENVO_01000886.definition: According to the NLCD 2011, areas of developed space under high intensity usage are dominated by constructed features where humans reside and work.  Examples include apartment complexes, row houses and commercial/industrial facilities. Further, it is asserted that "impervious surfaces", most likely referring to concrete and related substances, cover between than 80 - 100% of the area. Such thresholds - which are themselves fuzzy - are not strictly asserted in this definition.

ENVO_01000891.label: area of pastureland or hayfields
ENVO_01000891.definition: According to the NLCD 2011, at least 20% of these areas are covered by pasturelands or hayfields.  Such thresholds - which are themselves fuzzy - are not strictly asserted in this definition. The NLCD also notes that the crops are grown on a perennial cycle in these areas.

parents.label: area of gramanoid or herbaceous vegetation

ENVO_01000892.label: area of cropland
ENVO_01000892.definition: According to the NLCD 2011, at least 20% of these areas are covered by croplands or actively tilled land.  Such thresholds - which are themselves fuzzy - are not strictly asserted in this definition. The NLCD provides corn, soybeans, vegetables, tobacco, and cotton as examples of annual crops and the trees and vines in orchards and vineyards as examples of perennial woody crops.

ENVO_01001200.label: anthropised terrestrial environmental zone
ENVO_01001200.definition: A terrestrial zone which is bounded by constructed, manufactured, or other anthropogenic material entities.

ENVO_01001269.label: area of developed space
ENVO_01001269.definition: An area of a planet's surface which is primarily covered by constructed or manufactured objects and materials, possibly interspersed with cultivated or anthropically maintained vegetation.

ENVO_01001813.label: construction
ENVO_01001813.definition: A material entity which has been assembled through the intentional, instinctual, or deliberately programmed efforts of an organism or machine.

c_15203.label: vineyards
c_15203.definition: A vineyard is a plantation of grape-bearing vines, grown mainly for winemaking, but also raisins, table grapes, and non-alcoholic grape juice.

c_15911.label: organic agriculture
c_15911.definition: Holistic production management system which promotes and enhances agro-ecosystem health, including biodiversity, biological cycles and soil biological activity.
c_15911.definition_source: FAO. 2017. World Programme for the Census of Agriculture 2020. Volume I Programme, concepts and definitions. https://openknowledge.fao.org/handle/20.500.14283/i4913e
c_15911.scope_note: Agricultural methods without use of chemical products

c_16170.label: clearfelling
c_16170.scope_note: Removal of the entire standing crop

c_1872.label: coppicing
c_1872.definition: A silvicultural tool consisting of cut back trees or shrubs to ground level periodically to stimulate growth. The regrowth can be selected to facilitate forest regeneration.
c_1872.definition_source: Grazing with trees – A silvopastoral approach to managing and restoring trees. FAO Forestry Paper, No. 187, FAO, 2022 (https://doi.org/10.4060/cc2280en).

c_23fa0b98.label: permanent crops
c_23fa0b98.definition: Permanent crops are crops with a more than one-year growing cycle.
c_23fa0b98.definition_source: FAO. 2017. World Programme for the Census of Agriculture 2020. Volume I Programme, concepts and definitions. https://openknowledge.fao.org/handle/20.500.14283/i4913e
c_23fa0b98.scope_note: This category includes shrubs intended for flower production, fruit trees and vines, but not trees intended for timber or log production. For perennials, including trees for timber, see <c_5696>. For permaculture, see <c_482ab123>.

c_25243.label: grazing
c_25243.definition: Feeding on standing vegetation, as by livestock or wild animals.

c_2763.label: extensive farming
c_2763.definition: A system of raising crops and animals, usually on large parcels of land, where a comparatively small amount of production inputs or labor are used per acre.

c_28112.label: primary forests
c_28112.definition: Forest which has never been subject to human disturbance, or has been so little affected by hunting, gathering and tree-cutting that its natural structure, functions and dynamics have not undergone any changes that exceed the elastic capacity of the ecosystem.
c_28112.scope_note: Forests virtually uninfluenced by human activity

c_28144.label: secondary forests
c_28144.definition: Forest regenerated largely through natural processes after significant human or natural disturbance of the original forest vegetation.
c_28144.definition_source: Making forest concessions in the tropics work to achieve the 2030 Agenda: Voluntary Guidelines, FAO Forestry Paper No. 180, 2018 (http://www.fao.org/3/I9487EN/i9487en.pdf).

c_3120.label: fruit crops
c_3120.definition: Fruit crops are those yielding fruits and berries which generally are characterized by their sweet taste and their high content of organic acid and pectin.
c_3120.definition_source: FAO, 2024. Crops Statistics - Concepts, Definitions and Classifications https://www.fao.org/economic/the-statistics-division-ess/methodology/methodology-systems/crops-statistics-concepts-definitions-and-classifications/en/
c_3120.scope_note: Bananas, plantains, grapes, dates and carobs are considered fruit crops by FAO, while nuts, olives, coconuts, melons and water melons are not considered fruit crops.

c_34007.label: fallow
c_34007.definition: The cultivated land that is not seeded for one or more growing seasons. The maximum idle period is usually less than five years.
c_34007.scope_note: Uncultivated agricultural land could be brought back into cultivation using the resources normally available on an agricultural holding. Related terms: For "abandoned land" use <c_6>.  For "fallow", use <c_34007>. For "marginal land", use <c_4603>.  For "unclaimed lands", use <c_0e0e555b>.  For "virgin land", use <c_8257>. For "waste land", use <c_16205>.

c_34891.label: rice fields
c_34891.definition: Any cultivation of rice (Oryza sativa), submerged or not. Includes rice-cum-fish cultures, which are mixes of rice cultivation and fish harvesting in the same ponds.
c_34891.definition_source: FAO. 2023. The world’s mangroves 2000–2020. Rome. https://doi.org/10.4060/cc7044en

c_35171.label: landfills
c_35171.definition: The oldest method of waste disposal for waste. Landfill sites are usually disused quarries and gravel pits.

c_3906.label: intensive farming
c_3906.definition: A system of raising crops and animals, usually on small parcels of land, where a comparatively large amount of production inputs or labor are used per acre.

c_3952.label: irrigated farming
c_3952.definition: An agricultural production method that meets the water requirements of crops through irrigation.
c_3952.definition_source: Translated from CNTERM. 2024. CHINESE TERMS IN AGRONOMY 2024. https://www.cnterm.cn/news/tzgg/202407/P020250909517921360798.pdf

c_49983.label: mining
c_49983.definition: The process of extraction of valuable minerals or other geologic materials from the Earth, usually from an orebody, lode, vein, seam, reef or placer deposit.
c_49983.definition_source: Adapted from FAO. 2023. The world’s mangroves 2000–2020. Rome. https://doi.org/10.4060/cc7044en  and FAOLEX. 2025. Glossary https://www.fao.org/faolex/

c_50c7fa97.label: dredging
c_50c7fa97.definition: Removal of sedimented bottom mud from a pond, drain, ditch or watercourse.
c_50c7fa97.definition_source: Arrignon, J. (1970) Aménagement piscicole des eaux intérieures. Paris, SEDETEC Eds. 643p. Clément, J-M. (coord.) (1981)Larousse agricole. Paris, Librairie Larousse.

c_6.label: abandoned land
c_6.definition: Abandoned land refers to real property, such as plots of vacant land, buildings, or other structures, whose owners have relinquished ownership rights. This can happen either voluntarily, through explicit statements, or involuntarily, through extended lack of use, failure to pay property taxes, or other obligations of property ownership as determined by state law. Unoccupied land refers to land that is undeveloped, unused, and has no structures or improvements built on it. It is essentially land that is not currently being used or inhabited by people.

c_6436.label: rainfed farming
c_6436.definition: Agricultural production methods that rely on natural rainfall.
c_6436.definition_source: Translated from CNTERM. 2024. CHINESE TERMS IN AGRONOMY 2024. https://www.cnterm.cn/news/tzgg/202407/P020250909517921360798.pdf
c_6436.scope_note: Arable cultivation relying solely on rainfall

c_877.label: benthic environment
c_877.definition: The ecological region at the lowest level of a body of water such as an ocean, including the sediment surface and some sub-surface layers.
c_877.definition_source: FAO. 2021. Ecosystem approach to fisheries implementation monitoring tool – A tool to monitor implementation of the ecosystem approach to fisheries (EAF) management. User manual. Rome. https://doi.org/10.4060/cb3669en (benthic habitat)

c_f9554e7c.label: soil sealing
c_f9554e7c.definition: Permanent covering of the soil surface with impermeable artificial materials, leading to non-reversible loss of soil and most of its ecosystem services
